purpose: Teach: 雅子/恵子/静香/直人/健一/和夫/篤/哉

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが御皇室の雅子様のニュースを観られた
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Father would watch the news about the Imperial Princess Masako.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Voice settles into memory—unhurried, almost distant. A gentle warmth beneath the wistfulness. Slight pause between thoughts, as if searching for what mattered most in that moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、お友達の恵子さんとよくお出かけしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, Grandpa—you and your friend Keiko used to go out together so often when you were young, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, knowing tone. A light smile in the voice. Gently teasing—not correcting, but inviting him further into memory. That quality of having heard the same stories many times and still delighting in them. Soft trailing affection on "dear."

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが妹の静香さんを可愛がられた
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Father was so fond of my younger sister Shizuka.
lines.style: Gentle reminiscence. A softer attack this time—the memory almost tender. The name lingers slightly, held with care. Voice keeps its distance, observing rather than performing emotion.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、直人兄さんと将棋を指されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, when you were young, you used to play shogi with your older brother Naoto all the time, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Bright, engaging tone. She's drawn him back into the pattern—almost playful in the shift. The question rises with genuine curiosity, as if she's heard this echo many times but it hasn't worn thin. Warm and patient.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは健一氏と同僚として働かれた
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Father worked as a colleague with Kenichi.
lines.style: Voice settles deeper into memory here. A touch of reverence—not for the fact itself but for the weight of it. Measured pacing. The names matter. Not quite sad, but carrying the quiet of time passing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、和夫兄さんとお酒を酌み交わされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, when you were young, you and your older brother Kazuo used to share drinks together so often, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warmth with an edge of gentle mockery—she's keeping him in the dance they've done together. A light laugh underneath the words. She remembers these things too, maybe even more than he does. Not testing him, but holding the thread.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは「篤実な方々と仲良くしなさい」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when you were young, Father used to say, "Keep close company with people of real integrity."
lines.style: The tone becomes quieter, more weighted. Reverence for the advice itself—the voice shifts to honor what his father taught him. A pause before the quote. Delivered as something passed down, something that still matters. Slight gravity on the final phrase.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、「快哉、つまり快哉!と叫ばれる」場面が多かったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa, when you were young, you used to shout "Kaisai!" with such joy all the time, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: A delighted, almost mischievous warmth. She's catching him in a happy memory—almost teasing. The word "kaisai" rises slightly with her delight at the image. Voice closes gently and tenderly, like she's settling into the evening with him.
